evidence: Type assignment matches the nature of each criterion and the shipped template format. (1) Gates: hro_gate_render (gates/render/judge.toml:17-24) and hro_gate_shared (gates/constraints/judge.toml:17-24) are type = "binary" under aggregation = "all_pass"; both are pass/fail outcomes (wrong password refused + seeded sign-in shows workspace; job+candidate created and read back in an independent Observer context). (2) Functional: all 39 criteria (hro_job_open ... hro_restart, functional/judge.toml:23-405) are type = "binary" with positive weights 0.5-2.5; each describes a concrete observable product rule (stage moves, refusals, undo conflict, unread counts, access control, restart persistence) ending 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.' A keyword scan for degree words (clear|readable|good|appropriate|intuitive|quality...) found only 'readable line naming who and what changed' (functional:263, hro_activity) which is an existence test, not a craft scale. (3) Polish: all 5 criteria (polish/judge.toml:17-60) are binary and grade discrete state-preservation behaviours with measurable conditions (draft text unchanged, document.activeElement retained, scroll not reset, same message within a few pixels via getBoundingClientRect, failed send keeps text and sends once, session-end re-prompt and per-user drafts). These are pass/fail behaviours, not degree-of-quality; template polish is binary too. (4) Visual: all 5 criteria (visual/judge.toml:17-90: hro_vis_type, hro_vis_color, hro_vis_layout, hro_vis_hierarchy, hro_vis_consistency) are type = "likert", points = 5, weight 1.2, each with a described anchor at every level 5/4/3/2/1 (e.g. hro_vis_type lines 25-29: '5: clear consistent type scale ... 1: typography broadly illegible or unstructured'). This matches the template visual format (likert points=5 with anchors) and staged-task-contract ('likert with points = 5 is allowed in scored dimensions'); likert appears only in a scored dimension, never in gates. (5) Prompts agree with types: visual/prompt.md:7,12,16 use 'Likert 1'/'raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero' and 'grade every criterion independently with its five anchors'; functional/prompt.md:13,53 and polish/prompt.md:12,18 use binary 0. No binary craft criterion (lost gradation) and no likert block with missing anchors exists. Internal annotation ('Likert we dont use in rewrdkit') is the documented known false positive in SKILL.md:65 / quality-checks.md:170; judged against shipped template format, likert presence is not a defect. Adversarial probes: (a) plausible broken app passing - an app with weak but functional visuals gets partial likert (e.g. 3/5) rather than full credit, and a dead/static app is forced to Likert 1 by the visual browser gate (visual/prompt.md:11-12), so type choice does not let a bad app pass; a functionally broken app cannot collect binary credit from a craft scale because functional/polish are behaviour checks. (b) conforming alternative failing - a coherent but bold palette might score 4 rather than 5 on hro_vis_color's 'restrained distinct accents' anchor; that is a degree-of-quality gradation, which is exactly what likert is for, and loses at most a fraction of 0.2 visual weight, not a type-fit defect. Polish binaries use measurable tolerances ('within a few pixels', 15 s) rather than taste, so a conforming alternative layout is not failed for style.
notes: Static type/anchor fit only. No configured judge run exists in the raw evidence index, so actual rewardkit handling/normalization of likert points=5 (raw 1 -> 0) is unmeasured; that belongs to grading-wiring and reward-discrimination/ranking rows and their runtime records, and this row does not claim it. Visual has 5 likert criteria vs template 6 (no responsive row), consistent with visual/prompt.md:14 'No phone layout or theme switching is required'; not a type-fit issue.
